subject: Interim proxy shift + account-specific reroute steps (US/EU/APAC)
messages:
From: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
To: Anika Rao <anika@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Interim proxy shift + account-specific reroute steps (US/EU/APAC)

Hi Anika —

Quick update and immediate steps for Acme while we continue work on the underlying peering issue that impacted us-east1 and eu-west1 last night. We are proactively applying an interim proxy shift to move traffic for your tenants to alternative regions (us-west and eu-central) to reduce error rates and keep latency within your SLA targets.

What we will do (high level):
- Apply an account-scoped proxy rule that routes read/write requests to the dedicated fallback pool in us-west (primary) and eu-central (secondary).
- Enable a short TTL on cached prefixes so clients see the change in ~30s.
- Preserve logs and traces: we will mirror request logs to your existing S3/Log destination — no ingestion changes required on your side.

Account-specific actions you can take (optional, basic):
1) If you have a region preference in your client config, set REGION_PREFERENCE=us-west,eu-central.
2) If you call the API directly, switch the host to api-us-west.redwood.com for immediate effect.
3) If you depend on a DNS-based endpoint, add a temporary CNAME to api-us-west.redwood.com with TTL=30.

We attached a short runbook (interim_proxy_runbook.pdf) and the patch we intend to apply for Acme (acme-bridge-config.patch). Links: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-runbook.

Timeline: we can apply the interim shift within 20–30 minutes after you confirm. We will keep the change reversible and monitor error rates and latency for 6 hours; if stable, we will extend and coordinate a scheduled permanent reroute during a maintenance window.

Questions I expect: SLA credits, logs/retention impact, and whether this will require client code changes (it won’t unless you opt to change the host).

Please reply with APPROVE and we’ll start the change. If you need Legal on the thread for credit language, feel free to loop them in — I cc’ed them here.

Thanks,
Priya Natarajan
Account Lead, Redwood Inference

If answers are straightforward we can reply APPROVE and you can proceed.

Adding technical notes and confirmation from ops side — we will apply the change if you confirm. Details for Acme: 

What we'll apply (exact):
- Proxy rule: route tenant IDs acme-* to fallback pool: cluster-us-west-02 then cluster-eu-central-01.
- Edge config: set header X-Redwood-Region-Fallback: us-west,eu-central (this is transparent to clients).
- DNS: add CNAME entry for acme-api.acme-retail.com -> api-us-west.redwood.com with TTL 30 (we can push this for you if you give DNS access).
- Logs: replication to your S3 bucket (s3://acme-logs/redwood/) will continue; no retention policy changes. Traces will include forwarded-region tag for audit.

Rollback plan: revert proxy rule (5–10s propagation) and clear the small prefix cache we set (TTL=30).

Impact to tokens/auth: none. No client-side token rotation required.

I’m attaching the actual patch we’ll apply (acme-bridge-config.patch). Rishi and I will monitor Postman and playback job runs for order flows immediately after the change.

Marissa Cole
Customer Success Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

- Logs: confirmed — historical logs and the S3 replication pipeline remain unchanged. You will see entries with forwarded-region tags but all original fields preserved.
- Auth: no token rotation required.
- Peering ETA: networking estimates 18–36 hours for the root peering fix; we will provide hourly health updates in the shared runbook.

If you reply APPROVE we will initiate the interim proxy shift now (expected window 20–30m). Marissa and Rishi will run the validation suite and I’ll send a confirmation thread once live with a short post-change checklist.

If Legal wants to confirm wording for a credit, we can start that separately — it’s not required to proceed with the interim shift.

Best,
